title: Retinol Night Cream for Beginners: How to Start Safely
ex: How to start a retinol night cream slowly, how retinol compares with niacinamide and peptides, and a gentler option if retinol is not for you.
rt: Retinol Night Cream for Beginners | Mirc Glow
rd: Retinol night cream for beginners: how to start slowly, retinol vs niacinamide and peptides, tips for mature skin, and when to stop. Plain, honest guidance.
quick: Start a retinol night cream with a low strength, two nights a week, on dry skin, and wear sunscreen every morning. Increase slowly over several weeks. Mirc Glow creams do not contain retinol; most of them contain niacinamide, a gentler alternative.
facts: Beginner retinol products are often around 0.1–0.3%.
Start with two nights a week and build up slowly.
Avoid retinol in pregnancy unless your doctor says otherwise.
Mirc Glow creams do not contain retinol.
